title: Guided Savings Console: operational log and reversible apply UX for batching & cache recommendations
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a focused Console experience that turns automated batching and KV cache recommendations into a guided, reversible operational flow. The feature will surface recommendation cards, an explicit diff preview for proposed config changes, and a chronological operational log (apply history + audit trail) that supports safe rollback and post-apply forensic analysis.
background: Optimize currently generates automated batching and caching suggestions, but customers need: 1) clearer diff previews that show expected latency/cost delta, 2) an operational log that ties who applied what and when (with metrics), and 3) first-class rollback UX that validates safety before/after reversion. Past support incidents showed customers manually reverting server-side settings and lacking traceability against rollout windows.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards render with concise rationale, potential savings estimate, and a risk tag (none/low/medium/high).
Diff preview shows concrete config changes (route-level batching params, cache TTLs/prefixes) and simulated token-level cost impact over 7/30-day windows.
Apply flow records an immutable audit entry with user, time, git-like patch, and pre/post sampling of latency/cost metrics.
Rollback flow allows 1-click revert to previous config and executes an automated safety checklist (validate compat, smoke test traffic) before finalizing.
Operational log UI supports filtering by route, model, user, and time range and links to the associated evaluation prompt set used for quality regression checks.
End-to-end tests cover happy path apply, rollback, and conflict scenarios (concurrent changes).
design_notes: Primary UX is a stacked card layout grouped by workload (route/model). Each card has three states: Suggested, Applied (with link to audit entry), and Rolled Back. Diff preview is a side-by-side compact patch view with inline tooltips for metric deltas. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/optimized-guided-savings. Design decision to prefer explicit patches over freeform JSON editing to reduce operator error. Accessibility: ensure diff colors have >=4.5:1 contrast and keyboard-first actions.
engineering_notes: Backend: extend recommendations service to emit canonicalPatch (UNIFIED PATCH) and precomputed savings projection keyed by tenant+route.
Apply path: create an apply job that captures pre-state snapshot, executes patch via config manager, runs smoke evaluator, and writes audit record to append-only store.

Rollback path: lookup latest snapshot for route, run compatibility checks (model variant, quantization param constraints), then apply reverse patch. If smoke tests fail, auto-retry with exponential backoff and notify operator.
Trade-offs: storing full pre/post snapshots increases storage but simplifies forensic analysis. Alternative (delta-only) discarded due to historical incident where base state was lost.
Instrumentation: emit events for telemetry (apply.started, apply.completed, apply.failed, rollback.started, rollback.completed).
test_plan: Unit tests for patch generation and compat heuristics.
Integration test that runs apply->smoke->metrics-assert on a synthetic route with canary traffic.
E2E UI test to ensure diff preview renders for complex nested batching configs.
Chaos test: simulate mid-apply infra failure and assert audit record marks 'partial-failure' and rollback is possible.
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature flagged to internal orgs and Trusted Beta customers (10 orgs).
Week 2: collect feedback, iterate on diff wording and rollback confirmation flows.
Week 3: enable for all console users in opt-in mode and monitor telemetry for failed applies > 0.5%.
Post-launch: auto-promote opt-in to default after 30 days if customer_reversion_rate < 2% and quality-regression alerts == 0.
open_questions: What exact retention policy for pre/post snapshots (30d vs 90d)? Security/compliance team preference?
Should we allow engineers to edit the generated patch before apply, or only accept/reject? (Current plan: read-only patch with advanced 'Override' gate requiring two approvers.)
How to present uncertain savings estimates (show confidence band or single point estimate)?
Do we wire this audit trail into enterprise SIEMs via webhook or export job?
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Aisha Kumar. Initial scope reviewed with Maya Chen and Ravi Patel.
2026-03-03: Design spike completed; prototype shows diff preview and stacked card layout. Figma link added.
2026-03-05: Engineering spike (ENG-28451) validated snapshot approach. Decided to store full pre/post snapshots for safety.
2026-03-08: PM review with Customer Success - added 'rollback smoke test' requirement after customer anecdote of silent quality regressions.
2026-03-11: Feature flag scaffolding merged (github.com/redwood/console PR #6472). First end-to-end apply test passing in CI but one flaky smoke test observed; assigned to ENG-29712.
2026-03-12: Legal confirmed 30-day snapshot retention is acceptable for majority of customers; enterprise tenants can opt-in to 90-day with signed agreement. Updated ticket.
2026-03-12: Maya scheduled demo for Trusted Beta cohort on 2026-03-18.
estimated_savings_example: Example: route 'chat-stream' projected to save 23% token cost (approx $1.9k/month) when switching from eager batching=256 to adaptive batching=auto+prefix-cache TTL=120s; projection computed over 30 days of traffic profile.
notes_for_support: Support playbook: 1) view audit entry -> shows user and patch; 2) if customer reports regression, initiate rollback from audit entry and follow smoke test checklist; 3) escalate to Eng on call if rollback fails. Playbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Guided+Savings+Support
